SE.fullName: Lag (2018:1937) om tillgänglighet till digital offentlig service

enforcement.responsibility: Granskar webbplatser, appar och tillgänglighetsredogörelser för offentliga aktörer.

statutory.description: Public service broadcasters and certain non-governmental organisations are outside the Act. Since the amendment by Lag (2025:992), the provision refers to lagen (2025:986) om public service.

Five types of content are outside the requirements: (1) live broadcasts of time-based media; (2) maps not intended for navigation, where the item carries a qualification about essential information on the map content being provided accessibly in another way, which is part of item 2 and not a separate item; (3) digital services from a third party that are neither funded or developed by, nor under the control of, the public actor; (4) reproductions of items in heritage collections that cannot be made fully accessible without significant obstacles; (5) digital services in the school system or special forms of education, or in certain pedagogical care, unless they belong to the essential administrative functions of the activity. The paragraph also empowers the Government to issue further exemptions under Directive (EU) 2016/2102 Article 1(4)(a), (b), (g) and (h); that is a delegation, not a further content type.
An actor may be exempted from the requirements in 10 and 11 §§ where meeting them would be unreasonably burdensome, assessed case by case.
11 § applies only to digital services first provided after 22 September 2020.

FR.note: Intern #63 (Juno, 2026-09-10): `sanctions` is deliberately absent. The sanction TYPE is established — art. R. 451-4 of the code de la consommation makes a breach "une amende relevant des contraventions de 5e classe", a criminal fine rather than an administrative penalty — but no amount was established against primary source, and the Sanction shape requires minAmount/maxAmount. US.fullName: Americans with Disabilities Act Title II - Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in State and Local Government Services (28 CFR Part 35)

enforcement.authorityName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
enforcement.responsibility: Enforces web accessibility requirements for state and local government entities under ADA Title II. Final rule published 2024-04-24.

sanctions.type: DOJ Enforcement / Private Lawsuit / Settlement Agreement
sanctions.description: Title II enforcement uses the Rehabilitation Act remedies (42 U.S.C. § 12133 → 29 U.S.C. § 794a): DOJ compliance reviews, investigations, and settlement agreements; private individuals can file lawsuits for injunctive relief and compensatory damages. ADA Title II has no fixed civil monetary penalty schedule — unlike Title III, there is no $75k/$150k cap at the statute level.
sanctions.example: DOJ has entered consent decrees requiring full WCAG 2.1 AA compliance within 12-24 months, plus damages to affected individuals (e.g. settlement agreements with state university systems, municipal transit authorities).

US.note: Final rule (28 CFR Part 35, 89 FR 31320): web content and mobile apps of state/local governments must conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA. Original compliance deadlines extended by DOJ Interim Final Rule (published 2026-04-20): entities serving 50,000+ population now by 2027-04-26; entities serving under 50,000 population (and special district governments) now by 2028-04-26. Comment period open until 2026-06-22. Technical standard (WCAG 2.1 AA) unchanged.

largeEntity.description: State/local governments serving populations of 50,000 or more (28 CFR § 35.200(b)(1)). Deadline extended from 2026-04-24 by DOJ Interim Final Rule published 2026-04-20 (Federal Register).

smallEntity.description: State/local governments serving populations under 50,000, and special district governments (28 CFR § 35.200(b)(2)). Deadline extended from 2027-04-24 by DOJ Interim Final Rule published 2026-04-20 (Federal Register).

US.fullName: Americans with Disabilities Act Title III, Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability by Public Accommodations and in Commercial Facilities (28 CFR Part 36)

enforcement.authorityName: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
enforcement.responsibility: Enforces accessibility requirements for places of public accommodation (hotels, restaurants, retail, healthcare, etc.) including their websites and digital services.

sanctions.description: Private plaintiffs can file lawsuits under 42 U.S.C. § 12188 (injunctive relief only — no damages in federal court; state laws may allow additional damages). DOJ can seek civil monetary penalties per 28 CFR § 36.504 — statutory base amounts are $75,000 (first violation) / $150,000 (subsequent), annually inflation-adjusted per 28 CFR Part 85 (Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act). Consult the latest Federal Register inflation adjustment notice for current amounts.
sanctions.example: Thousands of ADA Title III web accessibility lawsuits filed annually. Notable settlements include Domino's Pizza, Winn-Dixie, and major retail chains.

US.note: No final DOJ rule for web accessibility under Title III as of 2026-04. DOJ enforcement and private litigation under Title III frequently cite WCAG 2.0/2.1 Level AA as the technical reference in settlements and consent decrees (e.g. Robles v. Domino's Pizza, Gil v. Winn-Dixie), but no single standard is formally mandated by regulation — practice varies between circuits. Legal exposure is primarily through private lawsuits for injunctive relief (42 U.S.C. § 12188). NPRM for web accessibility was published 2024; final rule pending.

US.law: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973
US.fullName: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance (45 C.F.R. Part 84)

enforcement.responsibility: Enforces Section 504 obligations for recipients of HHS federal financial assistance. Investigates complaints, conducts compliance reviews, and may recommend suspension or termination of federal funding. WCAG 2.1 AA is the technical benchmark applied in OCR enforcement actions from the compliance deadline (45 C.F.R. § 84.85).

sanctions.description: HHS OCR may suspend or terminate federal financial assistance for non-compliant recipients. Section 504 also provides a private right of action — individuals with disabilities may file lawsuits for injunctive relief and compensatory damages. No fixed statutory cap on damages; amounts vary by circuit and case. OCR may also initiate compliance investigations and require remediation plans.
sanctions.example: Loss of Medicare/Medicaid funding is the primary financial risk for healthcare organizations. Private Section 504 lawsuits have resulted in settlements and injunctions requiring full WCAG compliance with monitoring periods.

US.note: Applies to private organizations — including hospitals, physician practices, federally qualified health centers, long-term care facilities, health plans, and research institutions — that receive federal financial assistance from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), directly or indirectly. HHS administers over 100 programs, making the scope extensive. Medicare Part B reimbursements are considered federal financial assistance triggering Section 504 obligations. Five content exemptions exist: archived content, pre-existing conventional documents, individualized password-protected documents, pre-existing social media posts, and third-party content not controlled by the recipient. Does NOT cover federal agencies (see us-508) or state/local governments (see us-ada-title-ii). Rule published 89 FR 40066 (May 9, 2024); general Section 504 obligations effective July 8, 2024; WCAG 2.1 AA technical standards enforcement begins at compliance deadlines (15+ employees: 2027-05-11; <15 employees: 2028-05-10 — see complianceDeadlines). `effectiveDate` reflects the WCAG benchmark in-force date for the large-entity tier (the primary enforcement trigger); `inForce` flips to true on that date. Compliance deadlines were extended by one year via HHS Interim Final Rule (2026-09266), published in the Federal Register on May 11, 2026, with a 60-day public comment window closing July 6, 2026 (docket HHS-OCR-2026-0004). Technical standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) and scope are unchanged. Grundregeln är 89 FR 40066 av 2024-05-09, action "Final rule." Förlängningen av efterlevnadsdatumen är 91 FR 25496 av 2026-05-11, action "Interim final rule; request for comments." — samma dokument som dokumentnummer 2026-09266. Interim-lydelsen är alltså korrekt och ska inte ändras, men den dag en slutlig regel kommer blir den föråldrad samma dag och efterlevnadsdatumen måste läsas om.

largeEntity.description: Recipients of HHS federal financial assistance with 15 or more employees must conform web content and mobile apps to WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA (45 C.F.R. § 84.85). Deadline extended from 2026-05-11 by HHS Interim Final Rule published 2026-05-11 (Federal Register doc 2026-09266).

CA.note: Sanctions (Intern #93, Juno 2026-09-24): § 37(3) reads 'Every person who is guilty of an offence under this Act is liable on conviction, (a) to a fine of not more than $50,000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues to occur; or (b) if the person is a corporation, to a fine of not more than $100,000 for each day or part of a day on which the offence occurs or continues to occur.' The earlier range of 200 to 100,000 CAD is not in the Act. The field is removed rather than rewritten, because a single range cannot carry two per-day ceilings split by who is liable, and a flat maximum would understate an exposure that accrues per day. The two-element form, one per liable person, arrives with the sanctions schema in Intern #70.

CA.note: The Accessible Canada Act (ACA) is the federal accessibility statute, complementary to but distinct from provincial laws like AODA (Ontario), AMA (Manitoba), and similar. The Accessible Canada Regulations (SOR/2021-241) were amended to add specific ICT/digital accessibility requirements; the ICT amendments were registered and came into force 2025-12-05. The technical standard is CAN/ASC-EN 301 549:2024, the Canadian adoption of the EN 301 549 family (WCAG 2.1 Level AA baseline). Tiered enforcement: the Accessibility Commissioner at CHRC has primary jurisdiction; sector-specific enforcement is split with CRTC (broadcasting + telecom) and the Canadian Transportation Agency (federally-regulated transport). For US-style federal-vs-state context: this is the Canadian federal layer, complementary to provincial AODA-style laws. Annual progress reports were due from regulated entities by 2026-06-01 (passed). Sources: https://www.chrc-ccdp.gc.ca/organizations/accessible-canada-act-responsibilities/accessibility-deadlines and https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/programs/accessible-canada/regulations-summary-act.html Flyttat hit ur fullName (Intern #63/#66, 2026-09-12): Accessible Canada Regulations (SOR/2021-241), vars ICT-ändringar registrerades och trädde i kraft 2025-12-05. Lagens 1 § lyder "This Act may be cited as the Accessible Canada Act", alltså hör regleringen inte i namnfältet. Sanctions (Intern #70, Juno 2026-09-24): § 91(2) reads 'The maximum penalty in respect of a violation that may be fixed under regulations made under paragraph (1)(b) is $250,000.' The law makes no distinction between individuals and corporations. maxAmount 250000 is confirmed; the reference is § 91(2), not Part 6 as a whole.

enforcement.responsibility: Supervisory authority for EAA-covered digital services in Italy (art. 21 D.Lgs. 82/2022). AgID handles services oversight, complaints, and sanctions. Sector split per D.Lgs. 82/2022 + D.Lgs. 208/2021: MIMIT supervises products; AGCOM supervises audiovisual media services only. AgID operates a pre-istruttoria phase (codified in Determinazione n. 84 del 15 maggio 2026, 15 May 2026): on complaint or finding, AgID notifies the provider, requests a written response, and sets a remediation window before opening sanctioning proceedings. Sanctions are reserved for persistent non-compliance — the operative obligation for organisations is to have a documented response routine ready, not to assume immediate fines.

sectorAuthorities.responsibility: Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy — market surveillance for EAA-covered products (per D.Lgs. 82/2022). Does NOT supervise digital services.

Communications Regulatory Authority — surveillance and sanctioning only for audiovisual media services under art. 31 D.Lgs. 208/2021. Does NOT cover general digital services / e-commerce / banking / transport — those fall under AgID.

sanctions.description: Two distinct sanction ranges under D.Lgs. 82/2022: (1) substantive violation (non-compliance with accessibility requirements): 5,000–40,000 EUR per breach — this is the primary range exposed in minAmount/maxAmount; (2) non-cooperation / failure to comply with AgID orders during the pre-istruttoria phase: 2,500–30,000 EUR. Amounts within each range scale with severity, duration, and recurrence. AgID applies sanctions only after the pre-istruttoria response window has expired without remediation. Microenterprises providing services (under 10 employees AND ≤2M EUR turnover) are exempt — see exemptions.microbusiness.

microbusiness.description: Microenterprises providing services are exempt from accessibility requirements: organisations with fewer than 10 employees AND annual turnover or balance sheet at or below 2 million EUR. Both conditions must be met cumulatively. Microenterprises providing products are NOT exempt but qualify for relaxed obligations under EAA Annex IV.
microbusiness.legalBasis: Directive (EU) 2019/882 Article 4(5); microenterprise definition per Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC

IT.note: Italy transposed the EAA via D.Lgs. 27 May 2022, n. 82 (in force 28 June 2025). Authority split: AgID supervises digital services (websites, e-commerce, banking, transport, electronic communications, e-books) under art. 21; MIMIT supervises products; AGCOM supervises only audiovisual media services under art. 31 D.Lgs. 208/2021. The complaint mechanism (any party can file a non-compliance report via AgID's portal) is NOT new — it was established by Legge n. 4/2004 (Legge Stanca) and D.Lgs. 82/2022. Two 2026 AgID acts further the framework: (1) Determinazione n. 38 del 4 marzo 2026 (4 March 2026, in force 24 March 2026 via Gazzetta Ufficiale) — Linee Guida sull'accessibilità dei servizi digitali, structured checklists for websites/web apps, documents/office files, and mobile apps, based on EN 301 549 V3.2.1 + WCAG 2.1 AA; shifts the compliance perspective from individual web pages to entire digital services. (2) Determinazione n. 84 del 15 maggio 2026 (15 May 2026, GU 23 May 2026) — Regolamento sulle procedure di accertamento delle violazioni e applicazione delle sanzioni; codifies the pre-istruttoria phase (notification → response window → remediation period → sanctioning proceedings only on persistent non-compliance). Mandatory for operators in: e-commerce, banking and financial services, transport, electronic communications, audiovisual media services, e-books. Guideline source: https://www.agid.gov.it/sites/agid/files/2026-03/Linee_Guida_accessibilit%C3%A0_dei_servizi_(EAA).pdf Formal entry into force (Intern #63, Juno 2026-09-14): 2022-07-16. effectiveDate carries the date of application, 2025-06-28, because it drives inForce.
